items.headline: Haze risk rises as PSI nears unhealthy levels; NEA warns of a dry spell
items.summary: The National Environment Agency said haze risk could increase over the coming week as drier conditions build across the region. The 24-hour PSI reached 93 in the central area on Tuesday, just short of the unhealthy mark of 101, with hotspots detected over Sumatra.

items.headline: Messaging apps must get a user's consent before adding them to group chats
items.summary: Under new online-safety safeguards, platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram will need a user's consent before an unknown contact can add them to a group chat or channel. The measure is aimed at curbing scams and unsolicited or harmful content.

items.headline: Eleven arrested over a suspected unlicensed moneylending syndicate; over S$410,000 seized
items.summary: Police arrested eight men and three women aged 18 to 77 over their suspected roles in aiding an unlicensed moneylending syndicate. Officers seized more than S$410,000 and froze 29 bank accounts, and several of those arrested have been charged.

items.headline: Man, 59, taken back to Lengkok Bahru block where he allegedly murdered his neighbour
items.summary: Police escorted a 59-year-old man to the Lengkok Bahru block where he is accused of fatally stabbing his 59-year-old neighbour in July. The visit was part of continuing investigations into the killing.

items.headline: Protesters clash with police in Patna a month after India's Gen Z demonstrations
items.summary: Students and unemployed youth marched on the Bihar chief minister's residence in Patna, breaking through barricades as police used water cannon and batons. The unrest came a month after nationwide 'Gen Z' protests over jobs and governance.

items.headline: Porsche signs a $1.5 billion AI deal with Tata Consultancy Services
items.summary: TCS will set up a dedicated hub to run Porsche's AI deployment under a five-year contract worth about $1.5 billion. As part of the deal, TCS will acquire Porsche's IT consulting arm, MHP, for 320 million euros.

items.headline: UN watchdog urges India to curb caste violence and hate crimes
items.summary: A UN anti-discrimination committee said India must strengthen protections for tribal peoples and lower castes facing extrajudicial killings, torture and other abuses. It also called on New Delhi to act against hate crimes targeting Bengali-speaking Muslims.

items.headline: Update: India draws about $73 billion in 11 weeks to shore up the rupee
items.summary: New Delhi has attracted more than $73 billion in foreign-currency inflows over 11 weeks, nearly $65 billion of it through special deposits for non-resident Indians. The measures aim to steady a rupee weakened by a heavy oil-import bill and earlier capital outflows.

items.headline: Israeli forces raid a UNRWA training centre in occupied East Jerusalem
items.summary: Israeli forces, joined by far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, seized the Qalandiya vocational training centre run by the UN agency for Palestinian refugees in Kafr Aqab and raised an Israeli flag in its courtyard. UNRWA condemned the 'unauthorised' incursion, and at least five Palestinians were injured nearby.

items.headline: US threatens secondary sanctions on countries keeping economic ties to Iran
items.summary: Washington warned it could sanction any country or company that maintains economic links with Tehran, part of a shift toward economic pressure after recent strikes. China criticised the move and Iran vowed to retaliate.

items.headline: Zelensky says holding wartime elections could 'destroy' Ukraine
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky argued that staging elections while the war continues could 'destroy' Ukraine, pushing back on calls for a vote as Russian strikes persist. He said the country's focus must stay on defence and air cover.

items.headline: Iran's parliament advances a plan to charge transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iranian lawmakers moved forward with a proposal to levy service fees on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, as Tehran warned neighbours against joining a US-led economic campaign. About a fifth of the world's oil flows through the waterway.

items.headline: Apple launches a new Mac mini with the M6 chip, priced from $899
items.summary: Apple opened orders for a Mac mini built around its new M6 chip, which it says delivers up to four times the AI performance of the M4 model and adds a dual Neural Engine. Aimed partly at users running AI agents locally, it starts at $899 and is likely the last product launch of Tim Cook's tenure.

items.headline: Taiwan charges nine, including Nvidia and Supermicro staff, over AI-server exports to China
items.summary: Prosecutors in Taiwan indicted nine people for allegedly reselling Supermicro servers fitted with Nvidia's B300 chips to buyers in China, bypassing US and corporate export controls. Of 130 servers involved, 74 were said to have reached Chinese customers via Indonesia, Japan and Hong Kong.

items.headline: Broadcom seeks more than $60 billion in debt for an AI-chip deal tied to Anthropic
items.summary: Broadcom is in talks with lenders to raise over $60 billion, including a roughly $30 billion junior tranche, to finance AI chips for Anthropic and others. The size underscores the debt now fuelling the AI infrastructure build-out.

items.headline: AI-chip startup Fractile in talks for a $6.5 billion valuation after an Anthropic deal
items.summary: Fractile, which designs chips for AI and has agreed to supply Anthropic, is in advanced talks to raise about $600 million at a pre-money valuation of $6.5 billion. That would value it more than six times higher than a round it closed in May.

items.headline: Wall Street rises as the Dow logs a third straight gain while oil and yields fall
items.summary: US stocks advanced on Tuesday, with the S&P 500 closing at 7,677.28 and the Dow adding about 160 points for a third consecutive winning session. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.63% as investors awaited Nvidia's results and Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole address.

items.headline: Dick's Sporting Goods plunges about 30% in its worst day ever after cutting guidance
items.summary: Shares of Dick's Sporting Goods fell roughly 30% - its steepest single-day drop on record - after the retailer missed estimates and lowered its full-year outlook. It cited a challenging footwear market and a second-quarter loss at recently acquired Foot Locker.

items.headline: Canada unveils retaliatory tariffs on about $20 billion of US goods as a trade war escalates
items.summary: Canada said it would hit about $20 billion of US products - including steel, dairy, agricultural equipment and electronics - with new duties from Sept. 8, after Washington's 50% tariffs took effect and trade talks collapsed. Prime Minister Mark Carney vowed to respond 'dollar for dollar.'

items.headline: Oil drops sharply as the US pivots to economic pressure on Iran
items.summary: Crude fell about 3% to 4% on Tuesday, with Brent settling near $88.58 a barrel, as Washington leaned toward economic measures rather than fresh strikes on Iran, easing fears of an immediate supply shock.

items.headline: 🏏 India in command in Colombo as Sri Lanka trail by 238 on day three
items.summary: Prasidh Krishna took three wickets as India kept control of the second Test, reducing Sri Lanka to 265 for 8 in reply to India's first-innings 503 for 9 declared. Rain ended play early on day three, with the hosts still 238 runs behind.

items.headline: 🎾 Siniakova and Patten stun top seeds Sabalenka and Djokovic at the US Open
items.summary: Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten, through from qualifying, knocked out top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic in the first round of the revamped US Open mixed-doubles event. The upset headlined a day of surprises at Flushing Meadows.

items.headline: 🎾 Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reach the US Open mixed-doubles quarter-finals
items.summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz won eight of the last nine games to beat Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool 5-3, 4-1 and reach the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed-doubles event.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli leads the title race as Formula 1 pauses before Monza
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli tops the drivers' championship during the mid-season lull, with Lando Norris up to fourth after back-to-back wins in Budapest and Zandvoort. Formula 1 resumes at Monza on Sept. 6, where teams are expected to bring low-downforce upgrades.

items.headline: Physicists generate quantum entanglement using sunlight for the first time
items.summary: An international team produced entangled photon pairs using ordinary sunlight instead of a laser, reaching about 94% of a perfectly entangled state. Published in Optica, the approach could enable simpler, more energy-efficient quantum satellites and secure communications.

items.headline: New JWST images sharpen the debate over 'black hole stars' at cosmic dawn
items.summary: Fresh James Webb Space Telescope observations, including an X-ray detection, have intensified debate over 'black hole stars' - gas-shrouded early-universe objects whose light may be powered by a growing black hole rather than fusion. The findings bear on how the first supermassive black holes formed.

items.headline: A method to reverse cellular ageing is heading into human trials
items.summary: Researchers are preparing to test in people a technique that partially reprograms cells toward a younger state, an approach that has rejuvenated tissues in animals. Scientists caution that safety, especially cancer risk, will be the key question.

items.headline: Physicists pinpoint the ideal crystal site for an ultra-accurate nuclear clock
items.summary: By identifying the best position within a crystal lattice to host thorium-229 nuclei, researchers moved closer to a nuclear clock that could lose less than a second over the age of the universe. Such clocks could sharpen tests of fundamental physics.

fun_fact.headline: The Sahara was a green savannah with lakes as recently as about 5,000 to 11,000 years ago
fun_fact.body: The Sahara has not always been the world's largest hot desert. As recently as about 5,000 to 11,000 years ago, during the African Humid Period, much of it was green savannah threaded with lakes, rivers and wildlife - a “Green Sahara.” The shift was driven by a slow wobble in Earth's orbit that nudged the monsoon rains north.

puzzle.title: Brothers and Sisters
puzzle.body:
A man is looking at a portrait. Asked whose face it is, he replies:

“Brothers and sisters I have none, but this man's father is my father's son.”

Whose portrait is he looking at?
puzzle.approach: Work through the family relationships one link at a time, starting with 'my father's son.'
puzzle.answer:
His own son.

Since the speaker has no brothers, “my father's son” can only be the speaker himself. So the sentence becomes: “this man's father is me.” If the speaker is the man's father, then the man in the portrait is the speaker's son.

word_puzzle.title: Corner to Corner
word_puzzle.body:
A square has three letters on each side. Use every one of the 12 letters, spelling words where consecutive letters are on different sides; the last letter of one word begins the next. Target: solve it in just two words.

Top:     P · C · O
Right:   A · K · W
Bottom:  I · G · T
Left:    N · R · H
word_puzzle.approach: Each letter sits on one side of the square. Consecutive letters in a word must come from different sides, and a word's last letter starts the next word.
word_puzzle.answer:
PACKING → GROWTH

PACKING uses P-A-C-K-I-N-G and links on the final G to GROWTH (G-R-O-W-T-H). Together the two words use all 12 letters, and no word ever takes two letters in a row from the same side.
